name: What We Learn(ed) from Rainbows
description:
What can rainbows teach us about physics and mathematics?

As well as describing the beautiful physics of a dramatic natural phenomenon, rainbow studies over several centuries have uncovered unexpected connections with other areas of physics and the practice of science more generally. The connections encompass the rainbow as an illusion—there is no arc in the sky—rainbow-related waves in water, and the historical role of rainbows in shaping colour theory.

These connections extend even further, to the deeper conceptual transition from ray to wave optics. The talk will explore a variety of physics concepts, from wave optics to quantum mechanics, and how they link to rainbows: the universal wave decoration of smooth focal lines, decoherence—wave interference blurred by imperfect resolution, and Gell-Mann’s totalitarian principle.

Finally, the lecture will explore how rainbow bridges physics and advanced mathematics, serving as a laboratory for numerical experimentation when analytical solutions are insufficient and delve into the mathematics of divergent series.

name: Designing the Future
description:
How can art help us imagine possible futures?

Join Abel Korinsky for a collaborative crafting session, exploring how familiar materials and technologies might evolve into unexpected forms of life. Observe how everyday elements of the technosphere, be it plastic, electronics, or sensors, already shape our world and then speculate on what they could become.

Experimenting with motors, recycled plastics, and found materials, you will build a small moving organism of the future. Your speculative creatures might adapt to pollution, communicate with machines, survive in extreme environments, or develop entirely new relationships with humans and ecosystems.

name: Piece by Piece
description:
Puzzled by quantum? You’re in the right place. Join us for a relaxed afternoon to piece together quantum inspired puzzles of cats, wormholes, iridescence and more. You can also solve puzzles of beautiful images and even get a little competitive with some speed puzzling! 

Puzzles are for everyone: come alone, with a partner, or with friends and family!

name: Visualising Quantum Mechanics
description:
Quantum mechanics, like all of physics, aims to predict what happens, albeit in a probabilistic manner.  But what does it actually mean?  What is happening under the surface? Moving through a visual essay in your browser, you will examine this gap during the workshop. 

Vivek Vaidya will guide you through the hidden aspects of the double-slit experiment, decoherence, Bohm’s pilot wave, and the many-worlds interpretation. Between each topic, you play: aim a wavefunction at a target you cannot strike directly, read a barrier from a quantum-potential landscape, or herd thirty-two worlds that repel one another. The games use the same solvers as the essay figures, so the intuitions you develop reflect the physics.

name: D.D. Kosambi: One Life, Many Worlds
description:
Join us for a conversation around *D.D. Kosambi: One Life, Many Worlds*, Ramakrishna Ramaswamy’s biography of one of India’s most remarkable yet under-recognised intellectuals. Historian, mathematician, Marxist, and polymath, Kosambi’s work spanned mathematics, genetics, archaeology, literature, and the writing of Indian history.

The book launch session will feature a reading from the book, a moderated conversation with physicist Shashi Thutupalli, and an audience Q&A.

name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Mediators, Sushma and Nidhi, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: Unfolding Through Folding
description:
What can a sheet of paper teach us about the weirdness of the quantum world?

*Unfolding Through Folding* brings origami and quantum mechanics together in an unexpected, hands-on experience. Follow the folds, challenge your intuition, and discover how ideas that seem worlds apart can begin to make sense through something as simple as paper. The experience offers an intuitive, playful introduction to the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics.

The session will also feature a “cat in a box” origami model, specifically designed for the programme.

name: The Bengaluru Uncertainty Principle
description:
What does Bengaluru have to do with quantum physics? Quite a bit, as it turns out.

This quiz will explore the surprising connections between the city and the quantum world—from C. V. Raman and IISc to present-day quantum research, homegrown startups and a few unexpected detours through Bengaluru’s history and culture.

No physics degree required. The questions are designed to be beginner-friendly and workoutable, so curiosity and good guessing will take you a long way.

name: RECYCLERS: Urban Animation
description:
What happens when a wilted vegetable, a fallen leaf, or a forgotten spoon becomes a character?

In this hands-on stop-motion workshop, we’ll turn found objects and organic waste into curious characters, strange creatures and animated stories. Using vegetables, plants, leaves, stones and everyday food-related objects, join Nikki Schuster in bringing together a  stop-motion animation—turning the inanimate to life, one frame at a time.

name: Animated Realities: Experimental Animation and Documentary Filmmaking
description:
Nikki Schuster is the current BengaluREsidence artist at the Science Gallery. In this talk, she will present a selection of her experimental animation shorts and discuss her methodological approach to integrating experimental techniques into documentary filmmaking.

During her stay, Nikki explored emerging models of food production, urban farming, and local perspectives on soil and sustainability in Bengaluru, providing insight into her research process, fieldwork, and ongoing visual experiments.

name: Keeping Secrets in a Post-Quantum World
description:
What makes a secret impossible, or possible, to crack?

Come ready to crack codes, experiment with colour, and uncover the surprising ideas behind encryption. Join Rithvik Upadhya to take part in code-breaking games inspired by real events, to explore how information can be hidden in unexpected ways, and to discover how our methods of keeping secrets have evolved from ancient ciphers to the computers of today. We’ll also look ahead to quantum computers and how they could change the way we protect information.

No prior knowledge of physics, mathematics or computers is needed. The activities are designed to be fun and accessible, with plenty of room to get curious and dive deeper into the science and maths behind them. Whether you love puzzles, technology, or simply want to know how secrets are kept, there’s something here for you.

name: A Glimpse Into the Quantum World
description:
How did the quantum world change our understanding of reality and lead to quantum computing?

Join Arvind for a journey through the remarkable story of quantum physics, from the First Quantum Revolution and the birth of quantum mechanics to the emerging Second Quantum Revolution of today. Discover the counterintuitive world of superposition, measurement, and entanglement, and explore the landmark ideas of the EPR paradox, Bell’s inequalities, and their experimental verification. The talk will also highlight how quantum theory transformed technology through semiconductors, lasers, and superconductors, before turning to the exciting frontiers of quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum metrology.
